newsitem.title: USA: U.S. accounting board to issue guidelines on SAIF.
newsitem.headline: U.S. accounting board to issue guidelines on SAIF.

text.p: The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) will issue guidelines next week on how to account for payments to the Savings Association Insurance Fund which insures deposits at thrifts, an accounting executive said Friday.

FASB staff will release guidelines at next week's meeting of the Emerging Issues Task Force, according to Michael Crooch, chairman of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountant's accounting standards executive committee.
"I felt that this word ought to be out to the accountants and as a result I urged that the FASB staff make an announcement," Crooch said at an AICPA conference here.
A law enacted this Fall required thrifts to make a one-time payment to boost the Savings Association Insurance Fund (SAIF) to its mandated level.

Banks were then required to share with thrifts annual interest payments on Financing Corp bonds issued in the late 1980s to help with the thrift bailout costs. Those interest payments are made from premiums to the SAIF.
The accounting guidelines will confirm the current practice, Brian Smith, economic research director at America's Community Bankers, said. "There are really no surprises," he said.

The one-time special assessment was taken by thrifts as a third-quarter 1996 charge to operating income. Thrifts will receive a small rebate for fourth-quarter premiums which will be taken as an income or reduction expense item, Smith said.
Going forward thrifts and banks "will be doing essentially what we have done before ... recording the federal deposit insurance premium will be just a regular quarterly charge as you go," Smith said.
